source: Distilled from the append-only IDs in deleted_pieces.json plus explicit user rejection notes.
hard_constraints: Never use a tombstoned piece as a parent, reference exemplar, favorite, or gallery candidate.
Do not regenerate a deleted composition under a new title, palette, material, or object noun.
A technically functional render is not sufficient; reject work that reads as a Three.js demonstration or screensaver.
do_not_repeat: A single centered particle blob, sphere, vessel, bloom, antler, dome, tower, or other isolated sculptural noun floating on a dark background.
Cosmetic series generation where the same formal system is relabeled with neighboring nouns such as crown, bloom, antler, choir, tide, dome, bridge, chapel, hive, or tower.
Material substitution presented as conceptual evolution: glass, marble, weave, glow, fog, or bloom applied without changing spatial logic or meaning.
Generic cyan, amber, violet, or gold particles on black used as an automatic claim to atmosphere or sophistication.
Uniform ambient rotation, orbiting, breathing, pulsing, or noise drift with no irreversible event, consequence, or temporal argument.
Dense dots used to conceal weak silhouette, weak hierarchy, empty negative space, or an unreadable central form.
Blurry additive glow, self-occluding tubes, intestinal or vascular forms, and movement that resembles presentation-software animation.
Recognizable stock heads or faces with broken mouths, uncanny deformation, or no conceptual reason for portraiture.
Empty, CDN-dependent, shader-failed, interaction-gated, or nearly invisible opening states.
Poetic titles used to supply meaning that is not visibly present in the behavior or composition.
Decorative lines, trails, connectors, or scaffolding that have no legible structural or conceptual function.
Safe polished formal studies that vary surface styling but do not introduce risk, specificity, tension, or a legible artistic proposition.
required_countermoves: State the work's visible proposition in one concrete sentence before implementation.
Make composition, spatial relation, and temporal consequence materially different from every selected parent and recent sibling.
Use negative space and hierarchy deliberately; particle count cannot be the primary source of interest.
Make the first second legible, the fifth second deepen the premise, and the tenth second reveal consequence rather than repetition.
Reject sibling batches that differ mainly by title, object noun, palette, or material preset.
